name: Local and Air-Gapped Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped deployment covers AI systems that run on hardware the organisation controls, with no dependency on an outside network. In an air-gapped setup the machine is physically isolated, so no traffic reaches the public internet at all, while a local deployment may still sit on an internal network. The topic sits inside governance, risk and financial data security because it changes who can touch the data, the model and the logs. It applies to model inference, training runs, document processing and the surrounding storage and identity layers.

sections.body: Local and air-gapped deployment covers AI systems that run on hardware the organisation controls, with no dependency on an outside network. In an air-gapped setup the machine is physically isolated, so no traffic reaches the public internet at all, while a local deployment may still sit on an internal network. The topic sits inside governance, risk and financial data security because it changes who can touch the data, the model and the logs. It applies to model inference, training runs, document processing and the surrounding storage and identity layers.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The stack is ordinary data centre or workstation hardware: servers with sufficient GPU or CPU capacity, local storage, and a private network for anything that is not fully isolated. Models arrive as downloaded weights or as files carried across on approved media, and serving is handled by runtimes such as vLLM, Ollama or llama.cpp. Because there is no cloud control plane, patching, monitoring, backup and licence management all become internal responsibilities. Power, cooling and physical access controls matter as much as the software.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Teams typically start by classifying which data cannot leave the perimeter, then choose the smallest model that meets the task. Weights are transferred through a controlled process, checksummed, scanned and versioned, and the serving environment is built from a hardened image. Evaluation happens offline against a held-out set, and prompts, outputs and model versions are logged locally for later review. Updates follow a change process rather than a continuous pull, which slows release cadence but keeps the environment knowable.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main obligations are data residency, access control and auditability, and an air gap is one way to evidence that data never left the estate. That isolation also removes the vendor telemetry and cloud logging that many assurance teams rely on, so monitoring, incident response and retention have to be rebuilt in house. Model provenance still needs documenting: where the weights came from, what licence applies, and what data was used. Regulated firms should expect to show the same records for an isolated system as for a hosted one, and nothing here is legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Smaller open weight models and better quantisation keep widening what can run on modest hardware, which makes isolation practical for more workloads. Expect more tooling for offline model registries, signed weight distribution and local evaluation harnesses. The trade-off is that isolated systems age: they miss upstream safety fixes and drift from the vendor baseline. The likely direction is hybrid, with sensitive data and inference kept inside and only non-sensitive coordination crossing the boundary.
